Figure 1. Structure elucidation of 1. (A) Chemical structure of 1. (B) Single crystal X-ray structure of 1, with the cobalt-chelating moiety

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Inhibitory activity of 1 against coronavirus. (A) 1 exhibited
potent inhibitory activity against 3CLpro in vitro (IC50 8.1 μM). (B) 1
at 10 μM significantly reduced replication of live SARS-CoV-2 in a
Vero E6 infection model, comparable to the clinically approved
antiviral remdesivir. (C) 1 at 20 μM displayed no cytotoxicity against
the host Vero E6 cells. RLU: relative luminescence units; ns: not
significant; ****: p < 0.0001.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Structural analysis of 1 analogs based on MS/MS. (A) Predicted modifications in the motifs of monomer of 1 (1a representing the
monomer). (B) A selected view of the molecular network of analogs of 1a. The identified MOFs were divided into three groups and color-coded
based on their chemical properties. (C) Tentatively assigned structure of 1a’s analogs. (D) Characteristic MS/MS fragments of each structural
group.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Overview of isotopically labeled precursor incorporations of 1a. The independent yet parallel applications of isotopically labeled
precursor molecules, including L-threonine-15N, L-methionine-(methyl-13C), prenol-D6, glycerol-13C3, and L-valine-13C5, provided insights into the
biosynthetic origin of 1a. Incorporation of L-threonine-15N into the tetramic-acid ring (indicated as a blue triangle) suggests involvement of an NRP
pathway. The introduction of the N-methyl group (indicated as a blue dot) from L-methionine-(methyl-13C) further suggests a SAM-dependent N-
methyltransferase-mediated methylation step. Incorporation of deuterium-labeled prenol-D6 or 13C-labeled glycerol-13C3 into the terpene moiety
(deuterium incorporations indicated as red stars; 13C incorporations as red dots) confirms its terpene origin. The isobutyl moiety at the terminus of
the alkyl chain (indicated as green dots) originates from L-valine-13C5, consistent with a PK or fatty acid biosynthetic origin. All these labeling
assignments were established by comparing MS/MS fragmentation patterns between the isotopically labeled 1a and the unlabeled 1a (Figures S15
and S16). DMAPP: dimethylallyl diphosphate; MEP: methylerythritol phosphate.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. cbt BGC and proposed biosynthetic pathway for 1. (A) cbt BGC in S. davaonensis DSM101723 encodes a hybrid NRPS-PKS (CbtF and
CbtH−J) and four associated enzymes (CbtE, CbtG, CbtM, and CbtP) involved in the biosynthesis of 1. (B) Extracted ion chromatograms (EICs)
of sequential in vivo gene deletion of cbt BGC in the wild-type S. davaonensis DSM101723 (WT) suggest that CbtF and CbtH−J are involved in the
biosynthesis of 1. Disruption of terpene synthase-encoding genes (terA-E) in S. davaonensis DSM101723 did not affect production of 1. Each EIC is
normalized to the same scale. The analyses were repeated three times for each strain. ns: not significant compared to WT; n.d.: not detected. (C)
Hypothesized biosynthetic pathway for 1. DMAPP: dimethylallyl diphosphate.
